translations.literal: A jinshi of the first year of Zhi'ning, in office through prefectures and circuits he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of the Zhi'ning reign and earned a reputation for ability in successive prefectural posts.

sentences.zh: 歸德受兵，禹錫為行院都事，經畫寧禦一府倚重。

translations.literal: When Guide came under attack, Yuxi was secretary of the mobile headquarters and planned defense; the whole prefecture relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guide came under attack, Yuxi served as secretary of the mobile headquarters and planned its defense. The entire prefecture relied on him.

sentences.zh: 聞變，或勸以微服免，不從，見害。

translations.literal: When he heard of the disturbance, some urged him to escape in disguise; he refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the mutiny, some urged him to escape in disguise. He refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 是日蒲暮，官奴提兵入見，言：「石盞女魯歡等反，臣殺之矣。」

translations.literal: That day at dusk Guannu led troops in to see the emperor and said: "Shizhan Nülühuan and others rebelled; your servant has killed them."
translations.idiomatic: That evening Guannu led his troops in to see the emperor and reported, "Shizhan Nülühuan and others rebelled. I have killed them."

sentences.zh: 上不得已，赦其罪，以為樞密副使、權參知政事。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice but to pardon his crime and appoint him deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting councilor of state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to pardon him and appoint him deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting councilor of state.

sentences.zh: 初，官奴之母，自河北軍潰，北兵得之。

translations.literal: At the outset, when the Hebei army collapsed, Guannu's mother was captured by northern troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hebei army collapsed, Guannu's mother had been captured by northern troops.

sentences.zh: 至是，上乃命官奴因其母以計請和，故官奴密與忒木泬議和事，令阿裏合往言，欲劫上以降。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor ordered Guannu to use his mother as a stratagem to sue for peace; therefore Guannu secretly discussed peace with Temü, sent Alihe to speak, and wished to seize the emperor to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Guannu to use his mother as leverage to sue for peace. Guannu secretly negotiated with Temü, sent Alihe to speak with him, and plotted to seize the emperor and surrender.

sentences.zh: 忒木泬信之，還其母，因定和計。

translations.literal: Temü believed him, returned his mother, and thereby settled the peace plan.
translations.idiomatic: Temü believed him, returned his mother, and settled on a peace plan.

sentences.zh: 官奴乃日往來講議，或乘舟中流會飲。

translations.literal: Guannu then went back and forth daily to negotiate, sometimes meeting mid-river in boats to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Guannu went back and forth daily to negotiate, sometimes meeting mid-river in boats to drink together.

sentences.zh: 其遣來使者二十余輩，皆女直、契丹人，上密令官奴以金銀牌與之，勿令還營。

translations.literal: The more than twenty envoys he sent were all Jurchen and Khitan; the emperor secretly ordered Guannu to give them gold and silver tallies and not let them return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty envoys he sent were all Jurchen and Khitan. The emperor secretly ordered Guannu to give them gold and silver tallies and not let them return to camp.

sentences.zh: 因知王家寺大將所在，故官奴畫斫營之策。

translations.literal: Because he knew where the great general at Wangjia Temple was, Guannu therefore devised a plan to strike the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Learning where the Mongol commander at Wangjia Temple was stationed, Guannu devised a plan to strike his camp.

sentences.zh: 先是，忠孝軍都統張姓者，謂官奴決欲劫上北降，遂率本軍百五十人圍官奴之第，數之曰：「汝欲獻主上，我輩皆大朝不赦者，使安歸乎？」

translations.literal: Earlier, the Zhang-surnamed commander of the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army said Guannu was determined to seize the emperor and surrender north; he led one hundred fifty men of his army to surround Guannu's residence and rebuked him: "You wish to hand over the sovereign—we are all men the Great Dynasty will not pardon; where could we return?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Zhang-surnamed commander of the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army, believing Guannu meant to seize the emperor and surrender to the north, led one hundred fifty of his men to surround Guannu's residence and rebuked him: "You wish to hand over the sovereign. We are all men the Jin will never pardon. Where could we go?"

sentences.zh: 官奴懼，乃以其母出質，雲：「汝等若以吾母自北中來，疑我與北有謀，即殺之。

translations.literal: Guannu was afraid and offered his mother as hostage, saying: "If you suspect me of plotting with the north because my mother came from there, kill her.
translations.idiomatic: Guannu was afraid and offered his mother as a hostage, saying, "If you suspect me of plotting with the north because my mother came from there, kill her.

sentences.zh: 我不恨。」

translations.literal: I will bear no resentment."
translations.idiomatic: I will bear no resentment."

sentences.zh: 張意稍解，既以好語與之約曰：「果如參政所言，今後勿複言講和，北使至，即當殺之。」

translations.literal: Zhang's mind was somewhat eased; he then made a friendly agreement with him: "If it is truly as the councilor says, from now on do not speak of peace again—when northern envoys arrive, they must be killed at once."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was somewhat reassured and made a friendly agreement: "If it is truly as you say, speak of peace no more. When northern envoys arrive, kill them at once."

sentences.zh: 官奴曰：「殺亦可，不殺亦可，奏而殺之亦可。」

translations.literal: Guannu said: "Killing is acceptable, not killing is acceptable, memorializing and then killing is also acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Guannu said, "Killing them is fine, sparing them is fine, and memorializing before killing them is also fine."

sentences.zh: 張乃退，官奴即聚軍北草場，自言無反情，今勿複相疑也。

translations.literal: Zhang then withdrew; Guannu immediately gathered the army at the northern meadow and declared he had no rebellious intent—let there be no more mutual suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang withdrew. Guannu gathered his troops at the northern meadow and declared that he harbored no rebellious intent and that they should suspect him no longer.

sentences.zh: 遂畫斫營之策。

translations.literal: He then devised the plan to strike the camp.
translations.idiomatic: He then finalized the plan to strike the Mongol camp.

sentences.zh: 五月五日，祭天。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month they sacrificed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month they sacrificed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 軍中陰備火槍戰具，率忠孝軍四百五十人，自南門登舟，由東而北，夜殺外提邏卒，遂至王家寺。

translations.literal: The army secretly prepared fire-lance weapons; leading four hundred fifty Loyalty-and-Filiality troops they boarded boats at the south gate, went east then north, killed the outer patrol soldiers at night, and reached Wangjia Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The army secretly prepared fire-lance weapons. Guannu led four hundred fifty Loyalty-and-Filiality troops, boarded boats at the south gate, went east then north, killed the outer patrol at night, and reached Wangjia Temple.

sentences.zh: 上禦北門，系舟待之。

translations.literal: The emperor attended at the north gate, moored a boat, and awaited them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waited at the north gate with a boat moored ready.

sentences.zh: 慮不勝則入徐州而遁。

translations.literal: If they did not prevail he planned to enter Xuzhou and flee.
translations.idiomatic: If the attack failed, he planned to flee to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四更接戰，忠孝初小卻。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch they joined battle; the Loyalty-and-Filiality force at first fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch battle was joined. The Loyalty-and-Filiality force fell back slightly at first.

sentences.zh: 再進，官奴以小船分軍五七十出柵外，腹背攻之。

translations.literal: Advancing again, Guannu with small boats divided fifty or seventy troops outside the palisade and attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing again, Guannu sent fifty or seventy men in small boats outside the palisade to attack from front and rear.

sentences.zh: 持火槍突入，北軍不能支，即大潰，溺水死者凡三千五百餘人，盡焚其柵而還。

translations.literal: Wielding fire-lances they burst in; the northern army could not hold and collapsed in great rout; those drowned numbered more than three thousand five hundred; they burned all the palisades and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wielding fire-lances they burst in. The northern army could not hold and collapsed in rout. More than three thousand five hundred drowned, and they burned the palisades before returning.

sentences.zh: 遂真拜官奴參知政事、兼左副元帥，仍以禦馬賜之。

translations.literal: Guannu was then formally appointed councilor of state and concurrent left deputy commander, and an imperial horse was bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Guannu was formally appointed councilor of state and left deputy commander, and an imperial horse was bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 槍制，以敕黃紙十六重為筒，長二尺許，實以柳炭、鐵滓、磁未、硫黃、砒霜之屬，以繩系槍端。

translations.literal: The lance design used sixteen layers of imperial yellow paper as a tube about two chi long, packed with willow charcoal, iron slag, magnetite powder, sulfur, arsenic, and the like, with rope tied to the lance end.
translations.idiomatic: The weapon used a tube of sixteen layers of imperial yellow paper about two chi long, packed with willow charcoal, iron slag, magnetite powder, sulfur, arsenic, and similar substances, with rope tied to the muzzle.

sentences.zh: 軍士各懸小鐵罐藏火，臨陣燒之，焰出槍前丈餘，藥盡而筒不損。

translations.literal: Each soldier hung a small iron pot concealing fire; at battle they lit it, flame shooting more than a zhang before the lance; when the powder was spent the tube was undamaged.
translations.idiomatic: Each soldier carried a small iron pot with concealed fire. In battle they lit it, and flame shot more than a zhang beyond the muzzle. When the powder was spent the tube remained intact.

sentences.zh: 蓋汴京被攻已嘗得用，今複用之。

translations.literal: When Bian was besieged it had already proved useful; now it was used again.
translations.idiomatic: The weapon had already proved effective when Bian was besieged and was now used again.

sentences.zh: 兵既退，官奴入亳州，留習顯總其軍。

translations.literal: Once the troops had withdrawn, Guannu entered Bozhou and left Xi Xian to command his army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Mongol withdrawal Guannu entered Bozhou and left Xi Xian in command of his army.

sentences.zh: 上禦照碧堂，無一人敢奏對者，日悲泣雲：「自古無不亡之國、不死之君，但恨我不知用人，故為此奴所囚耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor attended at Zhaobi Hall; not one man dared memorialize; daily he wept in grief, saying: "From antiquity there has been no state that does not perish, no ruler who does not die—but I regret that I did not know how to employ men and am therefore imprisoned by this slave."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended court at Zhaobi Hall, but no one dared speak. Day after day he wept and said, "From antiquity no state has failed to perish and no ruler has failed to die. I only regret that I did not know how to employ men and am therefore imprisoned by this slave."

sentences.zh: 於是，內局令宋乞奴與奉禦吾古孫愛實、納蘭忔答、女奚烈完出密謀誅官奴。

translations.literal: Thereupon Inner Bureau director Song Qinu, attendant Wugusun Aishi, Nalan Keda, and Nüxilie Wanchu secretly plotted to kill Guannu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Inner Bureau director Song Qinu, attendant Wugusun Aishi, Nalan Keda, and Nüxilie Wanchu secretly plotted to kill Guannu.

sentences.zh: 或言，官奴密令兀惹計構國用安，脅上傳位，恢復山東。

translations.literal: Some said Guannu secretly ordered Wure to plot with Guo Yong'an, coerce the emperor to abdicate, and restore Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Guannu had secretly ordered Wure to plot with Guo Yong'an to coerce the emperor into abdicating and restoring Shandong.

sentences.zh: 事不成則獻上于宋，自贖反復之罪。

translations.literal: If the affair failed he would hand the emperor over to Song to redeem his crime of repeated rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: If the plan failed he would hand the emperor over to the Song to redeem his crime of repeated rebellion.

sentences.zh: 官奴以己未往亳州，辛酉，召之還，不至。

translations.literal: Guannu on the jiwei day went to Bozhou; on the xinyou day he was summoned back but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day Guannu went to Bozhou. On the xinyou day he was summoned back but did not come.

sentences.zh: 再召，乃以六月己卯還。

translations.literal: Summoned again, he returned on the jimao day of the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned again, he returned on the jimao day of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 上諭以幸蔡事，官奴憤憤而出，至於扼腕頓足，意趣叵測。

translations.literal: The emperor informed him of the plan to go to Cai; Guannu went out in rage, even wringing his wrists and stamping his feet—his intent was hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor informed him of the plan to relocate to Cai. Guannu left in a fury, wringing his wrists and stamping his feet. His intentions were impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 上決意欲誅之，遂與內侍宋乞奴處置，令裴滿抄合召宰相議事，完出伏照碧堂門間。

translations.literal: The emperor resolved to kill him and arranged matters with inner attendant Song Qinu, ordered Peiman Chaohe to summon the chief ministers to discuss affairs, and Wanchu lay in ambush in the doorway of Zhaobi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resolved to kill him. He arranged matters with inner attendant Song Qinu, ordered Peiman Chaohe to summon the chief ministers, and stationed Wanchu in ambush at the doorway of Zhaobi Hall.

sentences.zh: 官奴進見，上呼參政，官奴即應。

translations.literal: Guannu came in to audience; the emperor called "Councilor" and Guannu answered at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Guannu came in for audience the emperor called "Councilor," and Guannu answered at once.

sentences.zh: 完出從後刺其肋，上亦拔劍斫之。

translations.literal: Wanchu stabbed him in the ribs from behind; the emperor also drew his sword and hacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Wanchu stabbed him in the ribs from behind while the emperor drew his sword and hacked at him.

sentences.zh: 官奴中創投階下以走，完出叱忔答、愛實追殺之。

translations.literal: Guannu, wounded, threw himself down the steps to flee; Wanchu shouted at Keda and Aishi to pursue and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, Guannu threw himself down the steps to flee. Wanchu shouted at Keda and Aishi to pursue and kill him.

sentences.zh: 忠孝軍聞難，皆擐甲，完出請上親撫慰之。

translations.literal: The Loyalty-and-Filiality Army heard of the crisis and all donned armor; Wanchu asked the emperor to go personally to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: The Loyalty-and-Filiality Army heard of the crisis and donned armor. Wanchu asked the emperor to go personally and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 名呼李泰和，授以虎符，使往勞軍，因召范陳僧、王山兒、白進、阿裏合。

translations.literal: He called out Li Taihe by name, gave him the tiger tally, and sent him to comfort the army; he then summoned Fan Chenseng, Wang Shan'er, Bai Jin, and Alihe.
translations.idiomatic: He called out Li Taihe by name, gave him the tiger tally, and sent him to reassure the army. He then summoned Fan Chenseng, Wang Shan'er, Bai Jin, and Alihe.

sentences.zh: 進先至，殺之堂下。

translations.literal: Jin arrived first and was killed below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jin arrived first and was killed below the hall.

sentences.zh: 阿裏合中路覺其事，悔發之晚，為亂箭所射而死。

translations.literal: Alihe midway perceived the affair, regretted that he had acted too late, and was killed by stray arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Alihe realized what was happening midway, regretted acting too late, and was killed by stray arrows.

sentences.zh: 乞奴、愛實、忔答皆授節度使、世襲千戶，完出兼殿前右衛將軍，范陳僧、王山兒忠孝軍元帥。

translations.literal: Qinu, Aishi, and Keda were all granted military commissioner posts and hereditary commander of a thousand; Wanchu was made concurrent right guard general of the Hall Army; Fan Chenseng and Wang Shan'er were made commanders of the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army.
translations.idiomatic: Qinu, Aishi, and Keda were all appointed military commissioners with hereditary command of a thousand households. Wanchu was made concurrent right guard general of the Hall Army. Fan Chenseng and Wang Shan'er were made commanders of the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army.

sentences.zh: 於是，上禦雙門，赦忠孝軍以安反側。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor attended at the Double Gate and pardoned the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army to settle unrest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then attended at the Double Gate and pardoned the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army to settle the unrest.

sentences.zh: 除崔立不赦外，其餘常所不原者鹹赦之。

translations.literal: Except for Cui Li, who was not pardoned, all others ordinarily not forgiven were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Except for Cui Li, who was not pardoned, all others ordinarily excluded from amnesty were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 初，官奴解睢陽之圍，侍從官屬久苦饑窘，聞蔡州城池堅固、兵眾糧廣，咸勸上南幸。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Guannu relieved the siege of Suiyang, the attendant officials had long suffered hunger and distress; hearing that Caizhou's walls were strong and its troops and grain abundant, all urged the emperor to favor the south.
translations.idiomatic: When Guannu relieved the siege of Suiyang, the attendant officials had long suffered hunger and distress. Hearing that Caizhou had strong walls and abundant troops and grain, all urged the emperor to move south.

sentences.zh: 惟官奴以嘗從點檢內族斜烈過蔡，知其備禦不及睢陽，力爭以為不可，故號於眾曰：「敢言南遷者斬！」

translations.literal: Only Guannu, having once followed chief inspector of the imperial clan Xielie through Cai, knew its defenses did not match Suiyang's and argued forcefully that it was impossible; therefore he proclaimed to the crowd: "Whoever dares speak of moving south shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Only Guannu, having once followed chief inspector Xielie of the imperial clan through Cai, knew its defenses fell short of Suiyang's and argued forcefully against the move. He proclaimed to the crowd, "Whoever dares speak of moving south shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 眾以官奴為無君，諷上早為計，會其變，遂以計誅之。

translations.literal: The crowd considered Guannu disloyal to his sovereign and hinted to the emperor to act early; when his mutiny came they therefore killed him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd considered Guannu disloyal to his sovereign and urged the emperor to act. When his mutiny came they killed him by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 後遣烏古論蒲鮮如蔡，還言其城池兵糧果不足恃，上已在道，無可奈何。

translations.literal: Later they sent Wugulun Puxian to Cai; he returned saying its walls, troops, and grain truly could not be relied on; the emperor was already on the road and nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Later they sent Wugulun Puxian to Cai. He returned reporting that its walls, troops, and grain truly could not be relied on. The emperor was already on the road and nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 及蔡受兵，始悔不用官奴之言，特詔尚書省月給其母妻糧，俾無失所。

translations.literal: When Cai came under attack he began to regret not following Guannu's words and specially ordered the Secretariat to supply his mother and wife with monthly grain so they would not be destitute.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai came under attack he regretted not following Guannu's advice and specially ordered the Secretariat to supply monthly grain to Guannu's mother and wife so they would not be destitute.

sentences.zh: 習顯既黨官奴，一日率忠孝軍劫官庫金四千兩。

translations.literal: Xi Xian having sided with Guannu, one day led the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army to rob four thousand liang of gold from the government treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Having sided with Guannu, Xi Xian one day led the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army to rob four thousand liang of gold from the government treasury.

sentences.zh: 上命歸德治中溫特罕道僧、帥府經歷把奴申鞫問，顯伏罪下獄。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guide administrative supervisor Wentehan Daoseng and headquarters secretary Banushen to interrogate him; Xian confessed and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guide administrative supervisor Wentehan Daoseng and headquarters secretary Banushen to interrogate him. Xian confessed and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 官奴變，顯脫走，殺總領完顏長樂於宮門，殺道僧、奴申於其家，遂奔亳。

translations.literal: At Guannu's mutiny Xian escaped, killed overall chief Wanyan Changle at the palace gate, killed Daoseng and Nushen at their homes, and fled to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: During Guannu's mutiny Xian escaped, killed overall chief Wanyan Changle at the palace gate, killed Daoseng and Banushen at their homes, and fled to Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及官奴伏誅，詔點檢阿勒根阿失答即亳州斬顯及忠孝軍首領數人。

translations.literal: When Guannu was executed, an edict ordered inspector Aleigen Ashida to behead Xian and several Loyalty-and-Filiality leaders at once in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guannu was executed, an edict ordered inspector Aleigen Ashida to behead Xian and several Loyalty-and-Filiality leaders at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 兀惹使用安未還，伺于中路，數其罪殺之。

translations.literal: Wure had Yong'an return but had not yet come back; he waited on the road, enumerated his crimes, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an had not yet returned from Wure's mission. Wure waited on the road, enumerated his crimes, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 完顏承立

translations.literal: Wanyan Chengli
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Chengli

sentences.zh: 內族慶山奴，名承立，字獻甫，統軍使拐山之子，平章白撒之從弟也。

translations.literal: Of the imperial clan, Qingshannu, personal name Chengli, style name Xianfu, son of overall military commissioner Guaishan, younger cousin of chief minister Ba Sa.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshannu of the imperial clan, personal name Chengli, style name Xianfu, was the son of overall military commissioner Guaishan and younger cousin of chief minister Ba Sa.

sentences.zh: 為人儀觀甚偉，而內恇怯無所有。

translations.literal: In person his bearing was very imposing, yet inwardly he was timid and possessed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He had an imposing bearing, yet inwardly he was timid and lacked substance.

sentences.zh: 至甯初，宣宗自彰德赴闕，慶山奴迎見於台城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhi'ning, when Emperor Xuanzong came from Zhangde to the capital, Qingshannu welcomed him at Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhi'ning reign, when Emperor Xuanzong came from Zhangde to the capital, Qingshannu welcomed him at Terrace City.

sentences.zh: 宣宗喜，遣先還中都觀變。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was pleased and sent him back first to the central capital to observe developments.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was pleased and sent him back first to the central capital to observe developments.

sentences.zh: 宣宗既即位，以承立為西京副留守，權近侍局直長，進官五階，賜錢五千貫，且詔曰：「汝雖授此職，姑留侍朕，遇闕赴之，仍給汝副留守祿。

translations.literal: Once Xuanzong had taken the throne, Chengli was made Western Capital deputy defender, acting Inner Service Bureau director, advanced five ranks, and granted five thousand strings of cash; an edict also said: "Though you receive this post, for now remain to attend Us; when a vacancy arises go to it, and We shall still grant you the deputy defender's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuanzong had taken the throne, Chengli was appointed Western Capital deputy defender and acting Inner Service Bureau director, advanced five ranks, and granted five thousand strings of cash. An edict said, "Though you receive this post, remain for now to attend me. When a vacancy arises you may take it up, and I shall still grant you the deputy defender's salary.

sentences.zh: 此朕特恩，宜知悉也。」

translations.literal: This is Our special favor; you should understand it fully."
translations.idiomatic: This is my special favor. You should understand it fully."

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，遷武衛軍副都指揮使，兼提點近侍局。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was transferred to deputy commander of the Wuwei Army and made concurrent overseer of the Inner Service Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyou reign he was transferred to deputy commander of the Wuwei Army and made concurrent overseer of the Inner Service Bureau.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎專權僭竊，嘗為宣宗言之，後胡沙虎伏誅，慶山奴愈見寵倖，以為殿前右副都點檢。

translations.literal: Husahu monopolized power and usurped authority; he had once reported this to Xuanzong. Later when Husahu was executed, Qingshannu was increasingly favored and made right deputy chief inspector of the Hall Army.
translations.idiomatic: Husahu had monopolized power and usurped authority, and Chengli had once reported this to Xuanzong. After Husahu was executed, Qingshannu grew ever more favored and was appointed right deputy chief inspector of the Hall Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，大元兵圍中都，詔以慶山奴為宣差便宜都提控，率所募兵往援。

translations.literal: In the third year the Great Yuan army besieged the central capital; an edict made Qingshannu imperial commissioner and discretionary overall commander, leading recruited troops to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Mongol army besieged the central capital. An edict appointed Qingshannu imperial commissioner and discretionary overall commander to lead recruited troops to the relief.

sentences.zh: 俄為元帥右都監，行帥府事，兼前職。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made right deputy commander of the metropolitan command, exercising headquarters affairs, retaining his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made right deputy commander of the metropolitan command with authority over headquarters affairs while retaining his former post.

sentences.zh: 四年，知慶陽府事，兼慶原路兵馬都總管，以所獲馬駝進，詔諭曰：「此皆軍士所得，即以與之可也，朕安用哉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made superintendent of Qingyang Prefecture and concurrent overall chief of Qingyuan circuit military forces; he presented captured horses and camels; an edict instructed: "These were all obtained by soldiers—give them directly to the soldiers; what use has We for them?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed superintendent of Qingyang Prefecture and concurrent overall chief of Qingyuan circuit forces. He presented captured horses and camels. An edict instructed, "These were all obtained by the soldiers. Give them directly to the soldiers. What use have I for them?

sentences.zh: 後勿複進。」

translations.literal: Do not present such gifts again."
translations.idiomatic: Do not present such gifts again."

sentences.zh: 因令遍諭諸道帥府焉。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered this proclaimed throughout all circuit metropolitan headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The order was then proclaimed throughout all circuit metropolitan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 正大四年，李全據楚州，詔以慶山奴為元帥，同總帥完顏訛可將兵守盱眙，且令城守勿出戰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengda, Li Quan held Chuzhou; an edict made Qingshannu commander, together with overall commander Wanyan Eke leading troops to defend Xuyi, and ordered them to hold the city and not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 4, Li Quan held Chuzhou. An edict appointed Qingshannu commander, together with overall commander Wanyan Eke, to defend Xuyi with orders to hold the city and not give battle.

sentences.zh: 已而全軍盱眙界，二帥迎敵大敗，死者萬余人，委棄資杖甚眾，時軍無見糧，轉輸不繼，民疲奔命，愁歎盈路。

translations.literal: Shortly Quan's army reached the Xuyi border; the two commanders met the enemy and were greatly defeated—more than ten thousand dead, very many supplies and weapons abandoned. At the time the army had no visible grain, transport did not continue, the people were exhausted running errands, and lamentation filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan's army reached the Xuyi border the two commanders met the enemy and suffered a crushing defeat. More than ten thousand were killed and vast stores of weapons were abandoned. The army had no grain in sight, transport failed, the people were exhausted, and lamentation filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 諸相不肯正言，樞密判官白華拜章乞斬之以謝天下，不報。

translations.literal: The chief ministers would not speak plainly; Bureau of Military Affairs judge Bai Hua memorialized begging to behead him to appease the realm—the memorial went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers would not speak plainly. Bureau of Military Affairs judge Bai Hua memorialized begging to behead Qingshannu to appease the realm. The memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 降為定國軍節度使，又以受賂奪一官。

translations.literal: He was demoted to military commissioner of the Dingguo Army, and again lost one rank for accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to military commissioner of the Dingguo Army and lost one further rank for accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，鳳翔破，兩行省徙京兆居民于河南，令慶山奴以行省守之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Fengxiang fell; the two provincial headquarters moved Jingzhao residents to Henan and ordered Qingshannu to defend it with provincial authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year Fengxiang fell. The two provincial headquarters moved Jingzhao residents to Henan and ordered Qingshannu to defend the city with provincial authority.

sentences.zh: 時京兆行省止有病卒八百、瘦馬二百，承立懼不能守，屢上奏請還。

translations.literal: At the time the Jingzhao provincial headquarters had only eight hundred sick soldiers and two hundred thin horses; Chengli feared he could not hold it and repeatedly memorialized requesting to return.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao provincial headquarters had only eight hundred sick soldiers and two hundred thin horses. Chengli feared he could not hold the city and repeatedly memorialized requesting to return.

sentences.zh: 每奏一帖，附其兄白撒一書，令為地，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: With each memorial he attached a letter to his elder brother Ba Sa asking him to make room; the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: With each memorial he attached a letter to his elder brother Ba Sa asking him to secure his recall. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，慶山奴棄京兆還朝，留同知乾州軍州事、保義軍提控苟琪守之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Qingshannu abandoned Jingzhao and returned to court, leaving vice prefect of Qianzhou military affairs and Baoyi Army commander Gou Qi to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Qingshannu abandoned Jingzhao and returned to court, leaving Qianzhou vice prefect and Baoyi Army commander Gou Qi to defend it.

sentences.zh: 慶山奴行至閿鄉，哀宗遣近侍裴滿七斤授以黃陵岡從宜，不聽入見。

translations.literal: When Qingshannu reached Minxiang, Emperor Aizong sent attendant Peiman Qijin to grant him discretionary authority at Huangling Hill and did not allow him an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingshannu reached Minxiang, Emperor Aizong sent attendant Peiman Qijin to grant him discretionary authority at Huangling Hill and refused him an audience.

sentences.zh: 未幾，代徒單兀典行省事於徐州。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Tudan Wudian in exercising provincial authority at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Tudan Wudian as provincial authority at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，自徐引兵入援，選精銳一萬五千，與徐帥完顏兀論統之，將趨歸德。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he led troops from Xu to reinforce, selecting fifteen thousand elite troops and together with Xu commander Wanyan Ulun commanding them, intending to hurry to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he led troops from Xuzhou to reinforce the capital, selecting fifteen thousand elite troops under Xu commander Wanyan Ulun, intending to march on Guide.

sentences.zh: 義勝軍總領侯進、杜政、張興等率所部三千人降大兵。

translations.literal: Yisheng Army overall chiefs Hou Jin, Du Zheng, Zhang Xing, and others led their three thousand troops to surrender to the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Yisheng Army overall chiefs Hou Jin, Du Zheng, Zhang Xing, and others led their three thousand troops to surrender to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 慶山奴留睢州三日不敢進，聞大兵且至，懼此州不可守，退保歸德。

translations.literal: Qingshannu remained at Suizhou three days and dared not advance; hearing the great army was about to arrive, fearing the prefecture could not be held, he withdrew to defend Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshannu remained at Suizhou three days and dared not advance. Hearing the Mongol army was approaching and fearing Suizhou could not be held, he withdrew to Guide.

sentences.zh: 二月，行次楊驛店，遇小乃泬軍。

translations.literal: In the second month, marching to Yangyi Post, he encountered a small Naiwo army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, marching to Yangyi Post, he encountered a small Naiwo scouting force.

sentences.zh: 遂潰。

translations.literal: His force then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: His army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 兀論戰死，慶山奴馬躓被擒，惟元帥郭恩、都尉烏林答阿督率三百餘人走歸德。

translations.literal: Ulun died in battle; Qingshannu's horse stumbled and he was captured; only commander Guo En and commandant Ulinada Adu led more than three hundred men to flee to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Ulun died in battle. Qingshannu's horse stumbled and he was captured. Only commander Guo En and commandant Ulinada Adu led more than three hundred men in flight to Guide.

sentences.zh: 大兵以一馬載慶山奴，擁迫而行，道中見真定史帥，承立問曰：「君為誰？」

translations.literal: The great army carried Qingshannu on a single horse, pressing him along the way; on the road he saw the Zhending Shi commander and Chengli asked: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols carried Qingshannu on a single horse, pressing him along the road. En route he saw the Zhending commander Shi and Chengli asked, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 史帥言：「我真定五路史萬戶也。」

translations.literal: The Shi commander said: "I am Shi, commander of ten thousand of Zhending's five circuits."
translations.idiomatic: The commander replied, "I am Shi, commander of ten thousand of Zhending's five circuits."

sentences.zh: 承立曰：「是天澤乎？」

translations.literal: Chengli said: "Is it Tianze?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengli said, "Is it Tianze?"

translations.literal: He said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾國已殘破，公其以生靈為念。」

translations.literal: He said: "Our state is already shattered; my lord should have regard for the living people."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Our state is already shattered. Please have regard for the living people."

sentences.zh: 及見大帥忒木泬，誘之使招京城，不從，又偃蹇不屈。

translations.literal: When he met the great commander Temü, they tempted him to induce the capital to surrender; he did not follow, and again was arrogant and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When he met the Mongol commander Temü, they tried to induce him to persuade the capital to surrender. He refused and remained defiant and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 左右以刀斫其足折，亦不降，即殺之。

translations.literal: Attendants hacked his feet with blades until they broke; still he did not surrender, and they killed him at once.
translations.idiomatic: His guards hacked at his feet with blades until they broke. Still he would not surrender, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 議者以承立累敗不能解其軍職，死有餘責，而能以死報國，亦足稱雲。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Chengli, having repeatedly been defeated yet not removed from military office, deserved death many times over, yet in being able to die for the state he was also worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that Chengli, having suffered repeated defeats without being removed from command, deserved death many times over. Yet in dying for the state he was still worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 初，睢州刺史張文壽聞大兵將至，遷旁縣居民入城，大聚芻粟，然無固守意，日夜謀走以自便。

translations.literal: At the outset, Suizhou prefect Zhang Wenshou, hearing the great army was about to arrive, moved residents of neighboring counties into the city and gathered great stores of fodder and grain, yet had no intent to hold firm and day and night plotted escape for his own convenience.
translations.idiomatic: When Suizhou prefect Zhang Wenshou heard the Mongol army was approaching, he moved residents from neighboring counties into the city and gathered great stores of fodder and grain. Yet he had no intention of holding firm and plotted day and night to escape for his own convenience.

sentences.zh: 既而，聞承立人援，即以州事付其僚佐，托以應援徐兵，夜啟關契家走歸德，慶山奴以為行部郎中，死楊驛。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, hearing Chengli was coming to reinforce, he handed prefectural affairs to his subordinates, claiming he would meet the Xu troops in relief; at night he opened the gate and fled with his family to Guide. Qingshannu made him traveling department director; he died at Yangyi Post.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Chengli was marching to reinforce, he handed prefectural affairs to his subordinates, claiming he would meet the Xu relief force, then opened the gates at night and fled with his family to Guide. Qingshannu appointed him traveling department director. He died at Yangyi Post.

sentences.zh: 俄大兵圍睢州，以無主將，故殘破之甚也。

translations.literal: Shortly the great army besieged Suizhou; because there was no commanding general, it was therefore ravaged extremely.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol army soon besieged Suizhou. With no commanding general in place, the city was ravaged severely.

sentences.zh: 兀論，丞相賽不之侄，元光間例以諸帥為總領，兀論以丞相故獨不罷。

translations.literal: Ulun was the nephew of chief minister Saib; during Yuanguang it was customary to make the various commanders overall chiefs, but Ulun alone was not dismissed because of the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ulun was the nephew of chief minister Saib. During the Yuanguang period it was customary to replace commanders with overall chiefs, but Ulun alone was not dismissed because of his uncle's position.

sentences.zh: 金朝防近族而用疏屬，故白撒、承立、兀論輩皆腹心倚之。

translations.literal: The Jin court guarded against close kin and employed distant relatives; therefore Ba Sa, Chengli, Ulun, and their like were all trusted as intimate advisers.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court guarded against close kin and employed distant relatives. Therefore Ba Sa, Chengli, Ulun, and men like them were all trusted as intimate advisers.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：官奴素行反側，倏南倏北，若龍斷然。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Guannu's conduct was always treacherous, suddenly south and suddenly north, like a monopolist's grip.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Guannu's conduct was always treacherous, shifting suddenly south and north like a monopolist's grip.

sentences.zh: 哀宗一旦倚為腹心，終為所制，照碧之處，何異幽囚，其事與梁武、侯景大同而小異。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong once relied on him as intimate adviser, yet in the end was controlled by him; at Zhaobi Hall, what difference from secret imprisonment? The affair largely resembles Emperor Wu of Liang and Hou Jing, with minor differences.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong once relied on him as his closest adviser, yet in the end was controlled by him. At Zhaobi Hall he was no better than a secret prisoner. The affair largely resembles those of Emperor Wu of Liang and Hou Jing, with only minor differences.

sentences.zh: 徒單兀典、慶山奴為將皆貪，宜數取敗。

translations.literal: Tudan Wudian and Qingshannu as generals were both greedy; it was fitting they repeatedly met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Wudian and Qingshannu were both greedy as generals. It was fitting that they repeatedly met defeat.

sentences.zh: 女魯歡無大失行，而死於官奴，哀宗猶暴其罪，冤哉。

translations.literal: Nülühuan had no great misconduct, yet died at Guannu's hands; Emperor Aizong still exposed his crimes—how unjust!
translations.idiomatic: Nülühuan had committed no great misconduct, yet died at Guannu's hands while Emperor Aizong still publicly denounced his crimes. How unjust!
